# init merges its ignore lines into a .gitignore that already exists — every
# line of the existing file survives, and the second run appends nothing again.

env GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2
env GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=user.name
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=ambient
env GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=user.email
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=ambient@local

mkdir kb-dir
cp pre-gitignore kb-dir/.gitignore

exec akb init kb-dir
stdout '^Initialized KB "kb-dir" at .*/kb-dir$'

# The unrelated lines are kept and init's lines are appended after them.
cmp kb-dir/.gitignore gitignore-expected.txt
grep '^# host rules$' kb-dir/.gitignore
grep '^build/$' kb-dir/.gitignore
grep '^\*\.akb\.bak$' kb-dir/.gitignore
grep '^\.agent-kb/search\.db\*$' kb-dir/.gitignore

# A second run leaves the merged file byte-identical: no appended line is
# written twice. The initialized marker and the repository of the first run are
# cleared, so the second run starts where the first one did.
cp kb-dir/.gitignore gitignore-after-first.txt
rm kb-dir/.agent-kb kb-dir/.git

exec akb init kb-dir
stdout '^Initialized KB "kb-dir" at .*/kb-dir$'
cmp kb-dir/.gitignore gitignore-after-first.txt
cmp kb-dir/.gitignore gitignore-expected.txt

-- pre-gitignore --
# host rules
build/
tmp.cache
-- gitignore-expected.txt --
# host rules
build/
tmp.cache
*.akb.bak
.agent-kb/search.db*
